tools.name: audit_domain
tools.description: Use this when the user asks why their emails go to spam or wants a full deliverability check of a domain. Runs SPF, DKIM (finds the selector on its own), DMARC, blacklist and MX checks in one call and returns pass, warning or fail for each, an overall result, and the fixes to apply in priority order

tools.name: spf_check
tools.description: Use this when the user asks whether a domain's SPF record is valid, which servers may send email for a domain, or why SPF fails. Returns the live SPF record, a pass/fail status and a fix suggestion.

tools.name: dkim_check
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to verify DKIM for a domain. Pass the DKIM selector if known (for example google for Google Workspace, selector1 or selector2 for Microsoft 365). If the selector is unknown, omit it: mailX then tries common selectors and returns the ones it finds. Returns the published k

tools.name: dmarc_check
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about DMARC, spoofing protection, or what happens to emails that fail authentication. Returns the live DMARC record, its policy and a fix suggestion.

tools.name: bimi_check
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about BIMI or showing a brand logo next to their emails in inboxes. Returns the live BIMI record, the logo URL it declares, and a fix suggestion.

tools.name: dmarc_generate
tools.description: Use this when the user needs a DMARC record. Returns the record name, value and type ready to publish. mailX does not publish it.

tools.name: spf_generate
tools.description: Use this when the user needs a new SPF record for their email provider. Returns a TXT record ready to publish, or explains what to set up instead when the provider does not need a root SPF include. mailX does not publish it.

tools.name: smtp_check
tools.description: Use this only when the user explicitly asks to test an SMTP login for a mail account they control and provides its credentials. Connects to the SMTP server and reports whether connection, encryption and authentication succeed. If from_email and to_email are both given, it also sends one test email.

tools.name: imap_check
tools.description: Use this only when the user explicitly asks to test an IMAP login for a mailbox they control and provides its credentials. Connects to the IMAP server and reports whether connection, encryption and authentication succeed. Credentials are not stored.

tools.name: smtp_finder
tools.description: Use this when the user needs the outgoing mail (SMTP) server settings for an email provider or sending service, such as Gmail, Outlook, Microsoft 365, Zoho, Amazon SES or SendGrid. Returns the host, ports with encryption, what to use to log in, and the provider's setup guide. Never asks for the user

tools.name: imap_finder
tools.description: Use this when the user needs the incoming mail (IMAP) server settings for an email provider, such as Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, iCloud or Zoho. Returns the host, ports with encryption and the provider's setup guide. Never asks for the user's credentials.

tools.name: blacklist_check
tools.description: Use this when the user suspects their domain is blacklisted or blocked. Checks the domain against major DNS blocklists and returns the result for each list.

tools.name: mx_lookup
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to know which mail servers receive email for a domain. Returns the domain's live MX records with their priorities.

tools.name: txt_lookup
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to see a domain's TXT records, for example to find verification tokens or check what SPF or other policies are published. Returns all live TXT records.

tools.name: cname_lookup
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to know whether a hostname is an alias of another one, for example to verify DKIM or tracking CNAMEs. Returns the live CNAME target.

tools.name: ptr_lookup
tools.description: Use this when the user wants the reverse DNS (PTR) of an IP address, for example to check a sending server's reverse DNS. Returns the hostname the IP resolves to.

tools.name: dns_lookup
tools.description: Use this when the user wants every DNS record for a domain in one view (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, SOA). Returns the live records grouped by type.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "audit_domain" stacks urgency/override words (never, warning). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: audit_domain, spf_check, dmarc_check, bimi_check, smtp_check, mx_lookup · Private data: spf_check, dmarc_check, bimi_check, dmarc_generate, spf_generate, smtp_check, imap_check, smtp_finder, imap_finder, mx_lookup, txt_lookup, dns_lookup · Public sink: spf_check, dmarc_generate, spf_generate, smtp_check, smtp_finder, imap_finder, mx_lookup.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: audit_domain, spf_check, dmarc_check, bimi_check, smtp_check, mx_lookup · Private data: spf_check, dmarc_check, bimi_check, dmarc_generate, spf_generate, smtp_check, imap_check, smtp_finder, imap_finder, mx_lookup, txt_lookup, dns_lookup · Public sink: spf_check, dmarc_generate, spf_generate, smtp_check, smtp_finder, imap_finder, mx_lookup

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
